market_holds: Spot 13.79 in the sealed baseline (18:09 UTC), inside a 13-15 range held since May. The 20-day run-up is -8.7% and the 5-day +2.8%. The front-expiry straddle implies a 10.7% event move, ATM IV 94, with mild put skew (+1.8 vol points) and a low put/call OI ratio of 0.24 (baseline). The last four real earnings reactions were -6.8% (Nov-25), +9.4% (Mar-26), -13.0% (May-26) and -4.0% (Aug-26), median about 8%, so the options price a little above the realised history. The baseline's own 8-row list mixes in non-earnings 6-Ks, such as the 2026-11-04 AGM notice. Consensus (Yahoo, read 2026-11-12) is Q3 EPS $0.21 from 3 analysts, cut 1 in the last 7 days from $0.22, and revenue $408M from 7. FY26 EPS is $0.84, which implies H2 EPS of about $0.49 against $0.35 in H1, so consensus already builds in a large H2 margin ramp. The FY26 guide (Q2 release, 2026-08-13) is TPV +60-70%, gross profit +25-30% on a $403M base and operating profit +27.5-32.5% on a $220M base, held unchanged in August while TPV and GP were raised. The stock fell on that. Short interest was 17.4M shares, about 10 days to cover, at the 2026-10-15 settlement (Equibles/FINRA). General Atlantic sold down in August (13D/A, 2026-08-19).
view: DLO trades on margin, not volume. Every recent print beat on TPV, and the stock moved on gross-profit take rate and operating leverage: down on take-rate compression in Nov-25, May-26 and Aug-26, up when operating profit grew 48% in the Mar-26 print. The one line that matters tonight is whether the operating-profit guide still holds. My arithmetic from the company's own figures: H1 operating profit was $116.9M, so the guide needs $164-175M in H2, which is +38% to +47% year on year after +15% in H1. The GP guide implies only $258-278M in H2 (+18% to +27%). With H2 GP of about $278M and opex near $58M a quarter (down from $63M in Q2 now that the World Cup marketing has rolled off), H2 operating profit comes to about $162M, which is the bottom of the guide or just under it. So the guide is reachable only with GP at or above the top of its range or opex falling further, which leaves a real chance of an operating-profit guide trim or a low-end steer. Consensus Q3 EPS of $0.21, about $73M of operating profit on my rough tax and finance assumptions, already sits close to that ramp, and the stock has spent three months discounting it. On the other side, the TPV guide implies H2 TPV of only +43% to +60% after +92% in Q2, so it looks conservative. Management attributed most of Q2's take-rate drop to one large merchant and FX. Argentina's peso was stable through Q3 (about 1,500-1,545 per dollar). Shorts are about 10 days of volume. A clean step-up in operating profit could squeeze the stock. I find no fresh, dated datapoint that settles which of these wins. The guide risk is visible from public arithmetic and is reflected both in the post-Q2 sell-off and in the 10.7% implied move. The direction is close to a coin, with a slight lean down because three of the last four margin-line reactions were negative and the guide arithmetic is tight.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line, whether the FY26 operating-profit guide holds, can be computed from public guidance. The stock has visibly traded on it since August, and consensus EPS already embeds most of the H2 ramp. On the other side sit a conservative TPV guide, a stable peso and about 10 days of short interest. I found no dated evidence that breaks the tie, so there is no mechanism the price lacks.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: If Q3 operating profit is at or above about $78M with opex under $58M and the operating-profit guide is reaffirmed or raised, the high short interest makes a large up-move likely. A guide trim to below 27.5% would make it a clear down.

self_critique: The down-lean rests on my own reading of a guide that management chose to hold in August with July in hand. Companies rarely hold a guide they expect to miss 4.5 months later, and DLO hit its 2025 guide. Opex could fall faster than I assume, since Q3-25 opex was only $47.7M. The conservative TPV guide could also produce a GP beat large enough to carry operating profit, and with about 10 days of short interest that would move the stock sharply up. On the other side, a pattern of three down reactions in four is thin and can lead to extrapolating the last reaction. Either case is enough to keep me at no recommendation.
approach_notes: P6 (find the line the stock trades on) and the own-arithmetic route in P3 did the work: rebuilding the H2 operating-profit requirement from the company's own figures defined the question in minutes. P4 helped me resist calling the guide risk unpriced, because consensus EPS shows the market has already modelled the ramp. Grey and worker routes had little to offer for a B2B payments name in the time available.
